excerpt_i18n.en:
The biggest illusion of the AI era is equating a demo with a product. A single prompt generates a beautiful page, you screenshot it and post it on social media, and it gets hundreds of likes. But when you actually take it to a client, they ask: Where are the other pages? Is the color scheme consistent? Is it adapted for mobile? Can you make a revision? The gap between a demo and a product lies in these very questions.

One month after the launch of Skywork 3.0, the revenue of Tiangong Super Agent tripled. Behind this growth is an increasing number of users treating Tiangong as a productivity tool for delivering results.

This shift is concretely reflected in user behavior data. Among all of Tiangong's output capabilities, Websites is the scenario where users engage most deeply. Users are not satisfied with generating a single page and leaving; instead, they continuously refine the same project—adding requirements, adjusting structures, starting over, and further detailing. Deep users average over 40 interaction rounds per single project, with many complex projects taking shape across multiple login sessions.

Most people, however, end their AI usage after just three rounds.

We found that this group of deep users interacts with Tiangong in a fundamentally different way. They are not here for Q&A—they are here to build: to construct something long-term, complex, and personal. These needs are ultra-long-tail and highly individualized, impossible to achieve in a single generation—only through repeated iteration.
excerpt_i18n.es: La mayor ilusión de la era de la IA es equiparar una demo con un producto. Un prompt genera una página bonita, la capturas de pantalla y la publicas en redes sociales, y obtienes cien "me gusta". Pero cuando realmente la llevas a un cliente, este pregunta: ¿dónde están las demás páginas? ¿Los colores son uniformes? ¿Está adaptada para móviles? ¿Se puede modificar una versión? Entre una demo y un producto, la diferencia radica en estas preguntas. Un mes después del lanzamiento de Skywork 3.0, los ingresos de Tiangong Super Agent se triplicaron. Detrás de este crecimiento, cada vez más usuarios utilizan Tiangong como una herramienta de productividad para entregar resultados.

excerpt_i18n.en: When the core issues of an industry begin to shift, old infrastructure quietly fails—AI is experiencing such a moment. In March 2026, the National Data Administration released a figure: China’s daily token call volume had reached 140 trillion. In April, the Stanford AI Index Report noted that inference costs had dropped 280-fold over the past two years. Gartner’s forecast indicated that by 2026, 40% of enterprises would embed AI agents into their business systems. Together, these numbers read like an announcement of a new era. Fang Lei, founder and chairman of JiuZhang Cloud, offered an analogy: the First Industrial Revolution began with Watt’s steam engine, but what truly defined that era was Ford’s assembly line—it turned a genius’s one-time inspiration into a product accessible to everyone. AI now stands at the exact same inflection point: the breakthroughs in large models over the past few years were the “steam engine moment,” and the real test now is whether that “assembly line” can be built. But how much of that “assembly line” has actually been built? Shift your gaze from the macro numbers and ask engineers who are deploying AI at scale—you’ll find the other side of the numbers is a set of unresolved issues: massive token consumption has not translated into real business success, development environments remain fragmented between local code and cloud-based computing power, and enterprises lack reliable tools to assess the true return on investment for AI projects.

On June 17, Alibaba launched HappyOyster 1.0, an open-world model product capable of real-time construction and interaction. This product deeply learns the state transition laws of the physical world, actively deducing causal chains from actions to feedback while maintaining long-term consistency between characters and environments. HappyOyster 1.0 features two core capabilities: World Exploration (Adventure) and Real-time Directing (Directing), with upgraded interactive functions including attack, jump, plot backtracking, and branching storylines. Users can generate an interactive, explorable, and real-time modifiable AI digital world with just one sentence or one image. HappyOyster 1.0 can be widely applied in industries such as interactive gaming, virtual companionship, interactive short dramas, cultural tourism experiences, and live streaming. The official website is now open for user registration at https://www.happyoyster.cn.
